 Election Day storms lead off a big November pattern shift 
 Front returns seasonable temperatures 
 By Max Crawford and Sarah Howard Published : Nov. 1, 2026 at 12:05 PM CST | Updated : 1 hour ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BRYAN, Texas (KBTX) - November started with an extra hour and an extra helping at the temperature table. Humid air and foggy mornings of the past couple days will likely continue through Monday, then the much-advertised Election Day storm system arrives by or before sunrise Tuesday.
 Election Day is almost upon us! Showers and a couple storms are possible, mainly in the morning. We'll see a decent push of fall air as well, but nothing too wild. (KBTX) A strengthening low digging across the Rockies will drag a cold front southeastward across Texas on Tuesday , making it our headline First Alert Weather Day .
 Tuesday’s main event: Election Day rain & a couple thunderstorms
 If you’re planning to head to the polls on Tuesday, keep the rain gear handy, especially early. Deep Gulf moisture surging inland combined with decent upper level energy should give us the highest coverage of rain we’ve seen in almost a month. We expect a solid line of scattered showers and thunderstorms (70%+ coverage) to march across the region from northwest to southeast over the course of the morning, perhaps spilling over into the afternoon farther southeast. Some lingering rain is possible behind the front, but our best chance at collecting 0.25-0.75″ comes with the main cluster along the front.
 Severe & Wind Threat: While the bulk of the severe dynamics stays focused to our north, it’s not impossible we find a brief severe wind gust ahead of and along the front 
 Heavy Downpours: With models hinting at a slower frontal progression, localized heavy rainfall and brief ponding are possible but not expected at this time. 
 Behind the front, cooler and noticeably drier air sweeps in Tuesday night, knocking overnight lows into the crisp mid-50s and holding Wednesday afternoon highs in the comfortable mid-70s.
 Election Day is almost upon us! Showers and a couple storms are possible, mainly in the morning. We'll see a decent push of fall air as well, but nothing too wild. (KBTX) More Rain Chances Ahead, But Tuesday Is the Main Bet
 Looking past midweek, the broader upper-level pattern remains unsettled. A weak shortwave trough sliding overhead keeps a slight 20% rain chance in the mix for Thursday, and another impulse could spark isolated showers (20%) into next weekend.
 However, none of these subsequent waves look to carry the punch, coverage, or moisture supply that Tuesday’s system brings—making Election Day by far our most widespread and reliable shot at rain over the next 7 to 10 days. Keep checking back with the First Alert weather team as we fine-tune the exact hour-by-hour timing for Tuesday!
